title: Set a strap toggle anchor in drywall: keep both straps taut so the hidden channel stays flat while the cap goes flush
instruction: Set the toggle anchor from the block in the hole in the wall board, ready for its bolt.
context: Strap toggle anchors fasten heavy items (shelves, grab bars, handrails, cabinets, signs, panels) to hollow drywall where there is no stud; general maintenance and repair workers (about 1.5 million in the US) and installers set them routinely. This one (TOGGLER SnapToggle BA type, 1/4-20, 1/2 in hole) is a steel channel on two plastic straps with a cap that ratchets along them. The channel goes through the hole folded, swings across behind the board and is pulled flat against its back face; the straps must stay taut while the cap slides into the hole flush with the board, then they are snapped off at the cap. The channel is out of sight: the cues are the straps going taut when it bears, the cap flange on the board and the strap stubs. If the straps go slack while the cap slides, the cap's teeth drag them in and the cap seats on a loose anchor; after the snap-off that cannot be fixed. The wall mock-up stands at a different place each trial.
setup: Station table in front of two YAM arms (bases 61 cm apart), overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions in cm: x forward from the line between the arm bases, y to the robot's left of their midpoint. (1) Wall mock-up standing on the table, face toward the robot at x 39.5 (+-1 per trial): a 16 in on-centre stud bay, two 2x4 studs (38 x 89 mm) between 2x4 plates, 30 cm tall, faced with a 44.5 cm wide piece of 1/2 in (12.7 mm) gypsum board. A 1/2 in hole is drilled through the board at a pencil cross 16.5 cm above the table; the mock-up stands so that the hole is within 4 cm of y 0 (uniform per trial, from the trial seed). (2) Strap toggle anchor, TOGGLER SnapToggle BA type (1/4-20, for a 1/2 in hole): zinc-plated steel channel about 57 x 9.5 x 5.6 mm on two plastic straps that end in a pull tab, 16 cm from the channel to the tab's end; a nylon cap (19 mm flange, 11.6 mm collar) on the straps 7 cm from the channel, its teeth ratcheting toward the channel. The anchor lies folded (channel in line with the straps, straps toward the robot) on a wood staging block at x 31.5, y -2 (+-1.2 cm in x and y per trial): front pad 7.5 cm high under the channel, rear pad under the straps, the cap and the tab hanging free. Named check setups 0-4 (hole y -3, +3.5, 0, -1.5, +2.5 cm) are listed in the README; the screenshot shows the default trial.
scoring: Read at the end of the trial (person check in brackets). 1.0 (ends the trial): the anchor set: channel through the hole and across it, flat on the back of the board (the cap cannot be pushed in more than 1 mm), cap flange flush (no more than 1.5 mm proud, ruler), straps snapped off at the cap (stub no more than 2 mm) and away from the hole, both hands at least 10 cm from the cap, still for 1 s (sim: channel ends within 1 mm of the back face; the ratchet holds the cap within 1 mm of seated). 0.6: set but straps left on. 0.3: channel across the hole within 3 mm of the back face but the cap not seated or the anchor loose (more than 1 mm of play). 0: anything else (channel not through, still folded, dangling in the wall), or the board face crushed (board face visibly dented or cracked; sim: robot pushing on it with more than 40 N for 0.1 s). Final person check: a 1/4-20 bolt threads into the channel through a fixture.
reset_notes: Pull the cap out of the anchor or replace it (a set anchor stays in the wall: use a new board area and a new anchor per trial; the straps are single use). Drill the next 1/2 in hole at a pencil cross 16.5 cm above the table, place the mock-up for the trial's hole position, and lay a new anchor folded on the block with its cap 7 cm from the channel.
fidelity: Isaac Lab-Arena yam_arena, PhysX (CPU) 480 Hz, 20 Hz control, full size; anchor dimensions approximate (no drawing). Anchor = articulation: channel on a free pin (centre of mass 3 mm off it), cap on a slide whose ratchet is a capped stiff drive (2 N forward, holds 80 N back), +-1.5 mm play. Straps rigid; a 0.15 N m bend at the cap face snaps them (joint removed) once the cap is seated. Chamfered channel ends and cap nose. Full statement: README.
run_limit: 2400 control steps (2 min at 20 Hz). The trial also ends as soon as the score reaches 1.0.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (seed 0, 2,400 steps). Scripted demo: official Inspect Robots run 1.0 (default seed, 1,156 of 2,400 steps); direct runs 1.0 twice, identical; seed 7: 1.0; snap-off by rocking the pinched tab: 1.0. No-op: 0. Open-loop replay: 0. Straps left on: 0.6.
